clue.text: Astute academician out to get thoroughly wet

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the first word plus the academician are put out of order

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy

explanation.surface: A clever professor goes outside and gets soaked to the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak something completely is a synonym for making it thoroughly wet.

clue.text: Hurt lover!

parts.note: read not as a wounded sweetheart but as someone who loves hurting, a person taking pleasure in cruelty

explanation.definitionFit: A person who enjoys inflicting pain is literally a lover of hurt.

clue.text: Some go into this to contact those who are late

definitions.text: Some go into this to contact those who are late

parts.words: Some go into this to contact those who are late
parts.note: 'the late' are the dead; a spiritualist medium enters a dazed state to commune with them at a seance

explanation.definitionFit: A medium at a seance falls into a hypnotic, half-conscious state to reach spirits of the dead.

clue.text: Will throb inside some birds

indicators.note: some here means part of the preceding words, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: A determined pulse beats within a few feathered creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' looks like part of the definition, but it takes some of the letters of 'throb inside'; 'Will' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The redbreast is a familiar small garden bird, so its plural names several birds.

clue.text: I've a secret preparation, used for an afternoon meal

indicators.note: a preparation is something made up, so the letters of the preceding words are made up afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confides a hidden recipe for something to serve at teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: The cups, saucers and pot set out for afternoon tea form a matching china set.

clue.text: The horses' place in the theatre

definitions.meaning: the compartments in a stable where horses stand
the seats on the ground floor of a theatre auditorium

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both stable compartments and the ground-floor seating in a playhouse.

clue.text: It's to see their purpose in travelling

definitions.text: It's to see their purpose in travelling

parts.words: It's to see their purpose in travelling
parts.note: describes holidaymakers whose whole reason for a journey is sightseeing

explanation.definitionFit: Sightseers travel for pleasure precisely in order to look at places.

clue.text: Not short of weapons!

parts.note: seems to mean well armed, but describes weapons that are not short: archery bows of great length

explanation.definitionFit: The English archer's tall bow was a weapon defined by its length.

clue.text: It's royal to go around alone

indicators.note: going around suggests the letters of the preceding words are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A monarch wanders about the place all by themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's own, without company, is a synonym for being alone.

clue.text: Exhausted down-and-out?

definitions.meaning: completely worn out, tired to the point of collapse
an idle, penniless loafer or someone who dodges debts

explanation.definitionFit: As two words it means utterly tired; as one word it is a slang term for a layabout or vagrant.

clue.text: Dug out of the ground whole, by the sound of it

definitions.text: Dug out of the ground whole, by the sound of it

parts.words: Dug out of the ground whole, by the sound of it
parts.note: 'whole' heard as 'hole': an underground passage is a hole excavated through the earth

explanation.definitionFit: An underground passage is a long hole excavated through earth or rock.

clue.text: Supported the proposal to be temporarily transferred

definitions.meaning: at a meeting, formally backed a motion after it was proposed
moved to another post or organisation for a limited period

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both backing a motion in debate and being lent to another department for a while.

clue.text: After the death sentence, was suspended here in old England!

definitions.text: After the death sentence, was suspended here in old England!

parts.words: After the death sentence, was suspended here in old England!
parts.note: 'suspended' reads as hanging: the upright post with an arm from which executed criminals were hung

explanation.definitionFit: An old gallows from which hanged bodies were displayed as a warning.

clue.text: Used for military movements of deep significance?

definitions.text: Used for military movements of deep significance?

parts.words: Used for military movements of deep significance?
parts.note: 'deep' is the sea: vessels carrying soldiers across the ocean

explanation.definitionFit: Vessels that carry soldiers by sea move armies across the deep.

clue.text: Apparently one pulling tusks to somewhere remote from common humanity

parts.note: elephant tusks are made of ivory
someone who pulls or tows something is a tower

explanation.surface: Something that hauls elephant tusks somehow ends up in a far-off place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' flags that the phrase is being read literally, not as a set expression.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a place of privileged seclusion, cut off from the practical concerns of ordinary people.

clue.text: A whole range of fresh crumpets

indicators.note: fresh suggests something newly made, so the letters of the following word are made anew

explanation.surface: A full assortment of newly baked teatime crumpets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges CRUMPETS; crumpets are British griddle cakes eaten toasted.
explanation.definitionFit: A full span of possibilities from one extreme to the other is a spectrum.

clue.text: Spanish fighter to study at University, or end it all

indicators.note: the word or is placed at the end of everything else, finishing it all off

parts.note: taken as written
in British usage one reads a subject at university
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spaniard torn between going off to college and committing suicide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end it all' looks like despair but says OR goes last; to 'read' a subject is the British way of saying to study it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter, especially one on horseback, in the Spanish bullring.

clue.text: Right up hole…

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Right up hole…' (8): only a definition, 'hole', survives; the ellipsis suggests the clue is cut short and no wordplay for the answer is present

clue.text: He'll make a lucrative claim after a strike

definitions.text: He'll make a lucrative claim after a strike

parts.words: He'll make a lucrative claim after a strike
parts.note: 'strike' is a find of gold or ore, not industrial action; the finder stakes a mining claim

explanation.definitionFit: A gold-seeker who finds a seam registers a claim to mine it.

clue.text: And right away from a sailor is a soldier!

indicators.note: away from tells us one letter is taken out of the sailor

parts.note: a mariner is a sailor

explanation.surface: Take one seafarer off the right-hand side and you have a fighting man.
explanation.definitionFit: A Royal Marine is a soldier serving with the navy.

clue.text: Made money, but not on paper

definitions.text: Made money, but not on paper

parts.words: Made money, but not on paper
parts.note: money produced as coins stamped in metal, rather than printed banknotes

explanation.definitionFit: Coins are struck at a mint, so coinage is money made other than by printing notes.

clue.text: Sorted out and put away

indicators.note: sorted out suggests the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Things were tidied up and put into storage.
explanation.definitionFit: Things kept in reserve for later use have been put away.

clue.text: Applause lifts depression!

definitions.meaning: shouts of approval from a crowd

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both shouts of approval and brightens someone's spirits.

clue.text: Can we get away with reading such literature?

definitions.text: Can we get away with reading such literature?

parts.words: Can we get away with reading such literature?
parts.note: books that let the reader get away from reality into fantasy

explanation.definitionFit: Light fiction offering an escape from everyday reality.

clue.text: Metal found in air and mud

indicators.note: to found metal is to melt and cast it, so the letters are recast

explanation.surface: Some metal is discovered in the atmosphere and in the dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like 'discovered', but in the foundry sense it recasts AIRMUD.
explanation.definitionFit: A radioactive metallic element discovered by the Curies.

clue.text: I enter the church to become a clergyman

indicators.note: enter says the letter goes into the church

parts.note: a minster is a large church, such as York Minster

explanation.surface: A man joins a church and is ordained.
explanation.definitionFit: A Protestant clergyman is called a minister of religion.

clue.text: Take life seriously!

parts.note: seems to be advice to be earnest, but read as taking someone's life in a grave way

explanation.definitionFit: Unlawfully killing someone is literally taking a life.

clue.text: Went up to a meeting of the Supreme Court initially, then finally finished

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the first letters of the two words

parts.note: finished means ended

explanation.surface: A judge rose to a sitting of the highest court, which then wrapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes S and C from 'Supreme Court'; 'meeting of' and 'then finally' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb or rise is to ascend, so went up is the past tense.
